question: Should ClickClack commit to owning a provider-neutral, persisted managed-channel reconciliation API as a long-term core contract?
rationale: The patch is materially new product surface: it adds an HTTP endpoint, SDK method, durable identity fields, migrations, and documented desired-state semantics. Correctness evidence cannot decide whether that permanent capability belongs in core.

options.title: Accept the core reconciliation primitive
options.body: Merge the provider-neutral API and treat its persisted identity, migration behavior, and SDK surface as supported compatibility commitments.

options.title: Keep reconciliation outside core
options.body: Decline the new durable API and let integrations coordinate through existing channel operations or a future extension boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept the core reconciliation primitive
recommendation.body: Merge the provider-neutral API and treat its persisted identity, migration behavior, and SDK surface as supported compatibility commitments.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership attribution could not be established safely from the available evidence.
